rows.verbatim: Any proposed exception or deviation shall be clearly identified in accordance with L.4 and L.8.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall clearly identify any proposed exception or deviation per L.4/L.8.

rows.verbatim: Narrative volumes shall be submitted as searchable PDF files.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall submit narrative volumes as searchable PDF files.

rows.verbatim: The Price Template and Master Requirements Traceability Matrix shall be submitted in their native Microsoft Excel formats.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall submit the Price Template and Master RTM in native Excel format.

rows.verbatim: Each file name shall identify the Offeror, volume, factor, and document name.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall name each file to identify Offeror, volume, factor, and document name.

rows.verbatim: Files shall open without a password, proprietary viewer, cloud service, external website, or Internet connection.
rows.normalized: Offeror's files shall open without password, proprietary viewer, cloud service, external site, or internet connection.

rows.verbatim: Proposal content shall not be incorporated by reference to marketing materials, external websites, prior proposals, or documents not included in the proposal.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall not incorporate proposal content by reference to outside materials.

rows.verbatim: The Government will not evaluate narrative content exceeding the stated page limitation.
rows.normalized: Narrative content exceeding the page limit will not be evaluated.

rows.verbatim: Attachments excluded from a page limitation shall not be used to provide narrative information that was required to be included within a page-limited volume.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall not use excluded attachments to provide narrative required within page-limited volumes.

rows.verbatim: Information contained in one proposal volume may be considered in evaluating another factor when the relationship is apparent; however, the Offeror remains responsible for submitting the information expressly required for each factor.
rows.normalized: Offeror remains responsible for submitting information expressly required for each factor.

rows.verbatim: Proposals shall be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Officer listed in the SAM.gov solicitation posting no later than the date and time specified in Block 9 of the SF-33.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall submit proposals electronically via email to the CO no later than the date/time in SF-33 Block 9.

rows.verbatim: The proposal shall be organized as follows:
rows.normalized: Offeror shall organize the proposal per the specified volume structure.

rows.verbatim: Page Limit: Twelve (12) narrative pages.
rows.normalized: Volume II (Factor 1) narrative is limited to twelve pages.

rows.verbatim: Submission Limit: Not more than three (3) projects and not more than two (2) narrative pages per project.
rows.normalized: Volume III (Factor 2) limited to 3 projects, 2 narrative pages per project.

rows.verbatim: Submission: Completed Attachment 2 – RFP Price Template in native Microsoft Excel format.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall submit completed Attachment 2 Price Template in native Excel format for Volume IV.

rows.verbatim: An optional price explanation, when necessary under L.7, shall not exceed two (2) pages.
rows.normalized: If an optional price explanation is provided under L.7, it shall not exceed two pages.

rows.verbatim: Narrative pages shall use 8.5-by-11-inch pages, margins of at least 0.75 inch, Arial font no smaller than 10 points, and legible tables and graphics.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall format narrative pages as 8.5x11, min 0.75in margins, Arial 10pt min, legible graphics.

rows.verbatim: Excluded conceptual drawing pages shall contain drawings, dimensions, legends, and brief explanatory callouts only.
rows.normalized: Excluded conceptual drawing pages shall contain only drawings, dimensions, legends, and brief callouts.

rows.verbatim: Volume I shall contain the following.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall include the listed items in Volume I.

rows.verbatim: Except where expressly stated otherwise in Section M, these items will not receive a comparative technical rating.
rows.normalized: Volume I items generally will not receive comparative technical rating unless Section M states otherwise.
Offeror shall include a signed cover letter with legal name, address, UEI, CAGE code, POC, acceptance period, and authorized signer.

rows.verbatim: A table of contents, list of submitted files, and acknowledgment of all solicitation amendments.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall include a table of contents, file list, and amendment acknowledgment in Volume I.

rows.verbatim: Completed Section K representations, certifications, and solicitation-specific statements, together with evidence of active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM).
rows.normalized: Offeror shall include completed Section K reps/certs and evidence of active SAM registration.
Offeror shall include an organization/teaming summary identifying prime, subcontractors, suppliers, design authority, integrator, and facilities.

rows.verbatim: The summary shall identify the principal responsibility of each major team member.
rows.normalized: The teaming summary shall identify each major team member's principal responsibility.

rows.verbatim: A consolidated Exceptions, Qualifications, Deviations, and Assumptions Matrix. If none apply, state “None.”
rows.normalized: Offeror shall include a consolidated exceptions/qualifications/deviations/assumptions matrix, or state 'None' if none apply.
For each exceptions-matrix entry, offeror shall identify the affected requirement, proposed treatment, reason, and impact.

rows.verbatim: For an Offeror that is other than a small business concern and for which a subcontracting plan is required, submit a Small Business Subcontracting Plan complying with FAR 52.219-9, Alternate II, and the applicable requirements of FAR Subpart 19.7.
rows.normalized: If offeror is other than small business and a subcontracting plan is required, offeror shall submit a plan per FAR 52.219-9 Alt II and Subpart 19.7.

rows.verbatim: A small business Offeror shall state that a subcontracting plan is not required.
rows.normalized: A small business offeror shall state that a subcontracting plan is not required.

rows.verbatim: The Offeror shall provide the information required below for Factor 1.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall provide the Factor 1 information specified below.

rows.verbatim:
The technical proposal shall concentrate on the information necessary to demonstrate:
1. The feasibility and technical credibility of the proposed vehicle concept;
2. The Offeror’s approach to collaborative design, first-article development, verification, testing, and approval; and
3. The Offeror’s capability to manufacture, support, and, if ordered, scale production of the approved configuration.
rows.normalized: Offeror's technical proposal shall focus on feasibility, design/first-article approach, and manufacturing/support capability.

rows.verbatim: Across the three Factor 1 technical subfactors, identify no more than five (5) material risks that the Offeror believes are most significant to successful contract performance.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall identify no more than 5 material risks across the Factor 1 subfactors.

rows.verbatim: The prime Offeror shall hold a current ISO 9001 certification at the time of proposal submission and shall maintain ISO 9001 certification throughout contract performance.
rows.normalized: Prime offeror shall hold current ISO 9001 certification at proposal submission and maintain it throughout performance.

rows.verbatim:
The submitted certification shall:
1. Identify the prime Offeror as the certified organization; and
2. Encompass quality-management activities applicable to the work the prime Offeror proposes to perform under this contract.
rows.normalized: The submitted ISO certification shall identify the prime offeror and cover applicable quality-management activities.

rows.verbatim: Certification held solely by a parent company, affiliate, subcontractor, supplier, teaming partner, or other entity that does not identify the prime Offeror as a certified organization will not satisfy this requirement.
rows.normalized: Certification not naming the prime offeror will not satisfy the ISO 9001 requirement.

rows.verbatim: The Offeror shall submit its current ISO 9001 certificate as an attachment excluded from the Factor 1 page limitation.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall submit its current ISO 9001 certificate as an excluded attachment.

rows.verbatim: Failure to satisfy the ISO 9001 minimum requirement will result in the proposal being rated Unacceptable under Factor 1 and ineligible for award, as provided in M.1.1.
rows.normalized: Failure to meet the ISO 9001 minimum requirement results in Unacceptable rating and ineligibility for award.

rows.verbatim: Provide a concise description and conceptual drawings sufficient to demonstrate the feasibility and technical credibility of the proposed approach to the Tier II MCPV.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall provide a description and conceptual drawings demonstrating feasibility of the Tier II MCPV approach.
Submission shall at minimum depict/describe trailer configuration, layout, workstations, egress, interfaces, and major systems integration.

rows.verbatim:
The ISO 9001 certification requirement is a minimum Pass/Fail requirement as described in M.1.1. It is not a
comparative discriminator among Offerors that satisfy the requirement.
rows.normalized: The ISO 9001 certification requirement is evaluated Pass/Fail, not as a comparative discriminator.
The Offeror must provide one engineering-feasibility table with proposed/preliminary values and margins for the listed parameters.

rows.verbatim: Identify the basis of estimate for preliminary values.
rows.normalized: The Offeror must identify the basis of estimate for preliminary values.

rows.verbatim:
Values that cannot reasonably be finalized before post-award design reviews may be identified as preliminary,
provided the Offeror explains the basis for the value and why sufficient design margin exists to support
successful final design.
rows.normalized: If a value is identified as preliminary, the Offeror must explain the basis for the value and why sufficient design margin exists.

rows.verbatim:
Identify any material assumptions, qualifications, exceptions, or dependencies upon which the proposed concept
relies, including significant proprietary, supplier, subscription, licensing, or other external dependencies
affecting the feasibility of the proposed design.
rows.normalized: The Offeror must identify any material assumptions, qualifications, exceptions, or dependencies affecting the proposed concept's feasibility.

rows.verbatim: Complete the Offeror-response columns of Attachment 3 – Master Requirements Traceability Matrix.
rows.normalized: The Offeror must complete the Offeror-response columns of Attachment 3 – Master Requirements Traceability Matrix.
The Offeror shall identify each requirement in the matrix as Comply, Exception, Not Applicable, or No Response Required.

rows.verbatim:
A detailed proposal reference and explanation are required for every Exception or Not Applicable entry and
for requirements specifically addressed in this Factor.
rows.normalized: The Offeror is required to provide a detailed proposal reference and explanation for every Exception or Not Applicable entry and for requirements specifically addressed in this Factor.

rows.verbatim: A separate narrative reference is not required for every routine Comply entry.
rows.normalized: The Offeror is not required to provide a separate narrative reference for every routine Comply entry.

rows.verbatim:
The Offeror’s signed proposal constitutes its commitment that each unqualified Comply entry will be satisfied
within the proposed firm-fixed prices and in accordance with the resulting contract.
rows.normalized: By signing the proposal, the Offeror commits that each unqualified Comply entry will be satisfied within the proposed firm-fixed prices and per the resulting contract.

rows.verbatim: The approach shall address, as applicable:
rows.normalized: Offeror's approach must address the listed items, as applicable.

rows.verbatim: Provide one integrated schedule showing, at a minimum:
rows.normalized: Offeror must provide one integrated schedule showing, at a minimum, the listed items.

rows.verbatim:
Describe the Offeror’s approach for progressing from award through written Government approval of an
approved, production-representative first article.
rows.normalized: The Offeror must describe its approach for progressing from award through written Government approval of the first article.
The Offeror's approach shall address the listed design-build and first-article execution elements.
The Offeror must provide one integrated schedule showing at minimum the listed events and dates.

rows.verbatim:
Explain how the FBI will participate in the design-review process and select among compliant alternatives
while the Contractor retains responsibility for the design and its firm-fixed-price performance obligations.
rows.normalized: The Offeror must explain how the FBI will participate in design reviews while the Contractor retains design and firm-fixed-price performance responsibility.
The Offeror must address the listed government-participation and design-responsibility topics.
The Offeror must describe the vehicle-specific quality and verification approach, including the listed elements (list continues onto next page).

rows.verbatim:
Clearly identify how the Offeror will maintain responsibility and control over work performed by
subcontractors and suppliers, including quality control and integration of their work into the final vehicle.
rows.normalized: The Offeror must clearly identify how it will maintain responsibility and control over subcontractor/supplier work, including quality control and integration.

rows.verbatim:
Describe the facilities, workforce, engineering, manufacturing, integration, quality, test, supplier, and
management resources the Offeror intends to use for this requirement.
rows.normalized: The Offeror must describe the facilities, workforce, and other resources it intends to use for the requirement.
The Offeror must clearly distinguish work to be performed by the prime, major subcontractors, principal suppliers, and other facilities.
The Offeror must address the listed production and lifecycle-support capability topics.

rows.verbatim:
The Offeror is not required to demonstrate that dedicated production capacity for all potential follow-on
trailers is presently reserved or idle.
rows.normalized: The Offeror is not required to demonstrate presently reserved/idle dedicated production capacity for follow-on trailers.

rows.verbatim:
Instead, demonstrate a credible approach for:
1. Successfully producing the first article; and
2. If ordered, scaling production to up to twelve additional production trailers while maintaining the
approved configuration, schedule, quality, traceability, and required vehicle-specific records.
rows.normalized: The Offeror must demonstrate a credible approach for producing the first article and, if ordered, scaling to up to twelve additional trailers while maintaining configuration, schedule, quality, and traceability.
The Offeror must identify the proposed key personnel functions (Program Manager, lead design/systems engineer, quality lead, and manufacturing/production lead) in one table.
For each key person, the Offeror must identify name (if known), role, decision-making authority, relevant experience, and expected availability.

rows.verbatim: Full resumes are not required.
rows.normalized: The Offeror is not required to submit full resumes for key personnel.
The Offeror must describe its proposed warranty and nationwide support approach covering the listed elements.
The Offeror must identify any aspect of the proposed solution depending on the listed external dependencies.

rows.verbatim:
For each material dependency, describe the nature of the dependency and the Offeror’s proposed approach for
maintaining Government access to, or supportability of, the vehicle over its expected service life.
rows.normalized: For each material dependency, the Offeror must describe the dependency's nature and its approach for maintaining Government access/supportability over the vehicle's service life.

rows.verbatim: Submit not more than three (3) recent projects performed by the Offeror or a proposed major subcontractor.
rows.normalized: The Offeror must submit not more than three recent projects performed by the Offeror or a proposed major subcontractor.
For each submitted project, the Offeror must identify the listed project information elements.

rows.verbatim:
Projects completed within six (6) years before the proposal due date, or ongoing projects with at least one year
of performance, will normally be considered recent.
rows.normalized: Projects completed within six years before the proposal due date, or ongoing projects with at least one year of performance, will normally be considered recent for evaluation purposes.

rows.verbatim: Submit a completed Attachment 4 – Price Template in native Microsoft Excel format.
rows.normalized: Offeror must submit a completed Attachment 4 – Price Template in native Microsoft Excel format.

rows.normalized: Offeror's prices shall be firm-fixed and shall include every cost necessary to satisfy the requirement unless separately reimbursable per the solicitation.

rows.normalized: Offeror shall identify all recurring fees, subscriptions, licenses, externally hosted services, or other recurring charges needed to operate, maintain, or support the proposed solution.
